common_name: Edelweiss Grape (Cold-Hardy White Wine and Table Grape)

planting.note: Plant dormant vines in early spring once soil is workable, training young growth up a stake to reach the trellis wire.

directions: Bred by Elmer Swenson and released by the University of Minnesota in 1980 from a complex labrusca-vinifera-riparia parentage, this early-ripening hybrid tolerates winters well below zero with minimal cane damage, making it a mainstay for northern growers who cannot overwinter vinifera. Clusters of pale green-gold berries carry a mild, foxy labrusca flavor and work equally well for fresh eating, juice, or a light, fruity white wine. It ripens very early in the season, one of the first hardy hybrids to mature, which suits short-season gardens. The vine is vigorous and productive, so cluster thinning in the early years helps avoid overcropping and improves fruit quality.
